ownership_reason: Only the scan in the gold sees the individual elements; when it meets a larger element it has to record both the value and its position. Without the position step the gold returns the start of the range whatever the elements are, so its output carries no information about where the largest value is: hop 1 can only read the value at the index it is given, and no one-line change of the range at hops 2-4 (shorter, shifted, or a rescan from the returned index) recovers it, because every range yields its own start. The sibling overloads NumberUtils.max(int[]/short[]/byte[]/double[]/float[]) keep a running maximum replaced by each larger element, as does ObjectUtils.max (first on ties, documented); testMaxInt/testMaxShort/testMaxByte/testMaxDouble (passing) feed the same inputs ({6, 9} -> 9, {-5, 0, 10, 5, -10} -> 10). Known bypasses (W13, not competing repairs): hop 1 returning ObjectUtils.max(toObject(array)) or hop 2 returning ArrayUtils.indexOf(array, ObjectUtils.max(ArrayUtils.toObject(array))), which discard hops 2-5 or 3-5.
